## Overview
The Library Management System is a cloud platform for public and academic libraries to catalogue physical and digital items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals. It enforces strict EU-only data residency and sub-800ms search performance SLAs.

## Key Elements
- Library Patrons and Staff (Actors)
- Frontend SPA and Mobile App (React / React Native)
- API Gateway (Spring Cloud Gateway)
- Core Domain Services (Java / Spring Boot)
- Search Engine (Elasticsearch / OpenSearch)
- Database (PostgreSQL with Read Replicas)
- Async Message Broker (Apache Kafka / RabbitMQ)
- Notification Service (Java / Spring Boot)
- External Systems: Stripe EU, LDAP/SAML IdP, AWS S3 EU-Central, University SIS, Third-Party Delivery, RFID Gates

## Relationships
- Patrons/Staff -> Frontend SPA (HTTPS)
- Frontend SPA -> API Gateway (HTTPS)
- API Gateway -> Core Domain Services (HTTP/gRPC)
- Core Domain Services -> Search Engine (REST/TCP)
- Core Domain Services -> Database (JDBC/PostgreSQL Protocol)
- Core Domain Services -> Message Broker (AMQP/Kafka Protocol)
- Message Broker -> Notification Service (AMQP/Kafka Protocol)
- Notification Service -> External Email/SMS Provider (HTTPS/REST)
- LMS -> Payment Gateway, AWS S3, Delivery Service (HTTPS/REST)
- University SIS -> LMS (SFTP/HTTPS)

## Technology Stack
- Java/Spring Boot ecosystem: Chosen for enterprise maturity and robust microservices/modular monolith support.
- Elasticsearch/OpenSearch: Selected to meet the 99th-percentile search response time constraint of <800 ms.
- PostgreSQL (EU-Central): Provides reliable relational data storage with read replicas compliant with data residency rules.
- Apache Kafka/RabbitMQ: Enables decoupled, asynchronous event-driven workflows for notifications and indexing.
- AWS S3 EU-Central: Secures digital catalog asset storage within EU boundaries.

## Rationale
This architecture uses EU-hosted infrastructure and localized read replicas to strictly fulfill the data residency mandate. Additionally, utilizing an asynchronous message broker and dedicated search cluster ensures high-performance catalogue queries under peak academic circulation loads.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides a public and academic portal for cataloguing physical and digital items, managing circulation, and offering self-service features. It utilizes a decoupled container architecture strictly pinned to the `eu-central-1` region to satisfy EU data residency and performance constraints.

## Key Elements
- Library Patrons and Staff (Users)
- Web Application (SPA) (React/TypeScript)
- API Gateway (Nginx / Envoy)
- Core Services Container (Spring Boot / Java)
- Search Container (Elasticsearch Cluster)
- Integration Service (Node.js / Python)
- Async Worker Container (Python / Celery or Java / Spring Batch)
- Message Broker (Managed RabbitMQ)
- Database (PostgreSQL Managed RDS)
- Cache / Session Store (Managed AWS Redis)
- File Storage Container (AWS S3 EU-Central)

## Relationships
- Patrons/Staff to Web Application: HTTPS via browser
- Web Application to API Gateway: HTTPS/REST
- API Gateway to Core & Search Containers: gRPC / internal REST
- API Gateway & Core Services to Redis Container: RESP over TLS
- Core Services to PostgreSQL: JDBC over TLS
- Core Services to Message Broker: AMQP/TLS
- Message Broker to Async Worker Container: AMQP/TLS
- Integration Service & Async Worker to AWS S3 & Stripe EU: HTTPS/REST
- PostgreSQL to Search Container: Debezium CDC via internal TCP/TLS

## Technology Stack
- React/TypeScript: Powers the frontend SPA hosted on an EU-Central CDN
- Spring Boot (Java): Provides scalable business logic for core catalogue and circulation
- Elasticsearch: Optimizes indexing and queries to meet the < 800ms 99th-percentile search SLA
- PostgreSQL (Managed RDS): Ensures transactional consistency for core records
- Managed RabbitMQ: Enables decoupled asynchronous event handling and webhooks
- Redis (AWS ElastiCache): Delivers sub-millisecond session validation and hot caching
- AWS S3 EU-Central: Secures digital assets and documents within the EU boundary

## Rationale
This containerized architecture decouples synchronous user requests from heavy background processing, protecting the system against cascading failures from external integrations like Stripe and SIS. Strict isolation of read models, caching layers, and region-locked managed services guarantees compliance with EU data residency while easily achieving the sub-800ms search performance requirement.

Web Application (SPA).analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides a catalogue, circulation, and self-service portal for libraries. The architecture ensures strict EU-only data residency and sub-800ms search performance.

## Key Elements
- Web Application (SPA) container (React/TypeScript)
- Router & Shell Component (`react-router`)
- Authentication State Component (Context API + `oidc-client-ts`)
- Catalogue & Search UI Component
- Circulation & Self-Service Component
- State Management & Caching Store (`TanStack Query`)
- Notification & Feedback Component (`React Toastify`)
- API Client / HTTP Interceptor Component (`Axios`)
- API Gateway (`Nginx / Envoy`)

## Relationships
- Library Patrons and Staff -> Web Application (SPA) via browser `[HTTPS]`
- API Client / HTTP Interceptor Component -> API Gateway via `[HTTPS/REST]`
- Authentication State Component -> API Gateway via `[HTTPS/REST]`
- Catalogue & Search UI Component -> API Gateway via `[HTTPS/REST]`

## Technology Stack
- React/TypeScript: Powers the frontend SPA for high interactivity
- TanStack Query: Optimizes data fetching and client-side caching for performance
- Axios: Centralizes HTTP requests and bearer token injection
- EU-Central CDN: Enforces strict EU data residency constraints

## Rationale
Client-side caching via TanStack Query and input debouncing achieve the 99th-percentile search response time under 800ms. Deploying exclusively to an EU-Central CDN satisfies mandatory EU data residency constraints.

## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. The system enforces strict EU-only data residency and meets high-performance search requirements.

## Key Elements
- Web Application (SPA) (React/TypeScript)
- API Gateway Container (Envoy)
- Geo-Routing & Compliance Filter (Envoy Component)
- Authentication Filter (Envoy Component)
- Rate Limiting Filter (Envoy Component)
- Transformation Filter (Envoy Component)
- Routing & Dispatcher Engine with Circuit Breaker (Envoy Component)
- Core Services Container (Spring Boot / Java)
- Search Container (Elasticsearch Cluster)
- Cache / Session Store (Managed AWS Redis)
- LDAP/SAML IdP

## Relationships
- Web Application (SPA) -> API Gateway (Geo-Routing & Compliance Filter): Ingress point for all client requests [HTTPS/REST]
- API Gateway (Geo-Routing & Compliance Filter) -> API Gateway (Authentication Filter): Forwards validated, geo-compliant requests [In-memory]
- API Gateway (Authentication Filter) -> LDAP/SAML IdP: Validates user tokens [HTTPS/OIDC]
- API Gateway (Rate Limiting Filter) -> Cache / Session Store: Checks rate limit counters [RESP over TLS]
- API Gateway (Transformation Filter) -> API Gateway (Routing & Dispatcher Engine): Translates JSON to gRPC [In-memory]
- API Gateway (Routing & Dispatcher Engine) -> Core Services Container: Forwards requests with circuit breaking [gRPC]
- API Gateway (Routing & Dispatcher Engine) -> Search Container: Routes search queries [gRPC]

## Technology Stack
- Envoy: Selected for API Gateway due to native gRPC support, dynamic service discovery, and filter chain architecture.
- WebAssembly (WASM) / Lua: Utilized for custom geo-compliance filtering at the gateway perimeter.
- Spring Boot / Java: Powers backend business logic in the Core Services Container.
- Elasticsearch Cluster: Provides low-latency search capabilities.
- Managed AWS Redis: Handles caching, session storage, and rate-limiting counters.

## Rationale
The Envoy-based API Gateway utilizes a modular filter chain to enforce EU data residency and security at the perimeter while optimizing internal communication via gRPC. This architecture ensures low latency to meet the sub-800ms search performance requirement.

Core Services Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloguing, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries within an EU-only data residency constraint. The core services container utilizes a modular Spring Boot architecture to deliver scalable business logic.

## Key Elements
* Catalogue Management Component (Spring Bean / Java)
* Circulation Engine Component (Spring Bean / Java)
* Search Orchestrator Component (Spring Bean / Java)
* Authentication/Authorization Component (Spring Security / Java)
* Notification & Event Dispatcher Component (Spring Event / Java)
* Transaction & Audit Component (Spring `@Transactional` / Java)
* External Containers: PostgreSQL RDS, Elasticsearch Cluster, Managed RabbitMQ, AWS Redis, AWS S3

## Relationships
* Search Orchestrator Component -> Search Container: Executes high-performance queries [REST over TLS]
* Circulation Engine Component -> Message Broker: Publishes domain events [AMQP/TLS]
* Transaction & Audit Component -> Database: Commits atomic operations [JDBC over TLS]
* Circulation Engine Component -> Cache / Session Store: Manages transient states [RESP over TLS]
* Internal Components: Communicate via [In-process Method Calls]

## Technology Stack
* Java & Spring Boot: Provides robust enterprise framework for core services
* Elasticsearch: Delivers high-performance sub-800ms search capabilities
* PostgreSQL (RDS): Ensures ACID compliance for transactional data
* RabbitMQ & Redis: Handle asynchronous messaging and session caching

## Rationale
This modular component structure isolates business logic and guarantees ACID compliance for circulation workflows. Offloading complex queries to Elasticsearch ensures the 99th-percentile search response remains under 800ms while strictly enforcing EU data residency.

Search Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Search Container component of the Library Management System delivers ultra-fast, secure catalogue searching for physical and digital items. It provides resilient, high-performance querying while strictly adhering to EU data residency requirements.

## Key Elements
- **Query Service Component**: Java / Spring Boot service handling incoming search requests.
- **Schema Validation & Sanitization Component**: Java / OWASP Validator protecting against query injection.
- **Encryption & Compliance Component**: Java / Spring Security enforcing TLS 1.3 and data masking.
- **Circuit Breaker & Fallback Component**: Resilience4j handling latency spikes and fallback results.
- **Indexing Worker Component**: Java / custom consumer processing asynchronous updates.
- **Index Lifecycle Management (ILM) Component**: Elasticsearch ILM managing index rollover and purging.
- **Search Engine Core**: Elasticsearch 8.x distributed cluster deployed across 3 availability zones.

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> Query Service Component [gRPC]
- Message Broker -> Indexing Worker Component [AMQP via Debezium CDC]
- Query Service Component -> Cache / Session Store [Redis Protocol]
- Query Service Component -> Search Engine Core [Transport Protocol / HTTP over TLS 1.3]
- Indexing Worker Component -> Search Engine Core [HTTP/REST over TLS 1.3]
- Search Engine Core nodes <-> Search Engine Core nodes [Transport Protocol / TCP 9300]

## Technology Stack
- **Java / Spring Boot**: High-performance backend foundation for query processing and validation.
- **Elasticsearch 8.x**: Distributed search engine delivering sub-second queries and built-in ILM.
- **Resilience4j**: Lightweight fault tolerance for circuit breaking and fallback execution.
- **Managed AWS Redis**: Low-latency caching layer for fast fallback search snippets.
- **AWS EU-Central (`eu-central-1`)**: Cloud infrastructure region enforcing mandatory EU-only data residency.

## Rationale
This architecture uses event-driven asynchronous indexing to remove write contention from the critical query path, ensuring the 99th-percentile search response stays below 800 ms. Pinning the Elasticsearch cluster and storage strictly to `eu-central-1` fulfills all EU data residency constraints.

## Overview
The Library Management System is a comprehensive solution for public and academic libraries to catalogue items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals. The Integration Service acts as a resilient, modular container that securely manages all external third-party communications within the EU.

## Key Elements
- Integration Service Container (NestJS / TypeScript)
- Integration Facade / Router (NestJS Module with Circuit Breaker & Retry Middleware)

- gRPC: Used for high-performance internal communication from core services
- MQTT & HTTPS/REST: Standardized protocols for IoT and external API integrations
- Resilience4ts: Implemented for circuit breaking and retry logic to prevent cascading failures

## Rationale
This modular NestJS architecture isolates external system volatility from core business logic while ensuring strict data residency compliance. The inclusion of a facade, circuit breakers, and localized regional deployment meets all performance and EU-only data constraints.

The Python 3.11 and Celery stack with non-blocking `asyncpg` efficiently handles I/O-bound background tasks without blocking core APIs. Five dedicated components ensure robust third-party synchronization, reporting, and GDPR compliance while strictly enforcing EU-only data residency.

## Overview
- Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation management, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries.

- AMQP 0-9-1 / AMQP/TLS: Secures internal messaging and communication protocols
- Prometheus / RabbitMQ Prometheus Plugin: Enables real-time queue observability and telemetry
- Terraform / RabbitMQ definitions JSON: Ensures declarative, immutable infrastructure management
- HTTPS / TLS: Secures management APIs, webhook ingestion, and log export

## Rationale
- Decouples synchronous HTTP ingestion from asynchronous processing to maintain high performance and search response SLAs under 800 ms.
- Enforces strict EU data residency and auditability through isolated queue management and secure TLS communication.

Database.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. Its database architecture ensures transactional consistency, EU data residency, and high-performance search support.

## Key Elements
* **Relational Data Store:** PostgreSQL Managed RDS engine storing core transactional entities.
* **Connection Pooler:** PgBouncer managing inbound database connections.
* **Read Replica:** PostgreSQL Replica handling read-heavy queries and reporting.
* **WAL Publisher:** Emits transaction logs for Change Data Capture (CDC).
* **Backup & Snapshot Manager:** AWS RDS Automated Backups enforcing region-locked recovery.
* **Audit & Security Monitor:** `pgaudit` capturing security events and query logs.
* **Database Schema Migration Engine:** Flyway or Liquibase for version-controlled schema evolution.

## Relationships
* **Core Services Container -> Connection Pooler:** `JDBC over TLS`
* **Core Services Container -> Read Replica:** `JDBC over TLS (Read-Only)`
* **Core Services Container -> Relational Data Store:** `JDBC over TLS (DDL execution)`
* **WAL Publisher -> Search Container:** `TCP/TLS stream (Debezium CDC)`
* **Primary Engine -> Read Replica:** `PostgreSQL Streaming Replication [TCP/TLS]`
* **Relational Data Store -> Backup & Snapshot Manager:** `Internal AWS Storage API over TLS`
* **Audit & Security Monitor -> File Storage Container:** `HTTPS / S3 API`

## Technology Stack
* **PostgreSQL Managed RDS:** Selected for ACID compliance, relational integrity, and robust extension support.
* **PgBouncer:** Utilized to prevent connection exhaustion under peak circulation loads.
* **Debezium:** Enables low-latency CDC to meet the <800ms search NFR.
* **AWS S3 EU-Central:** Secures encrypted backups and audit log archival within EU boundaries.
* **pgaudit:** Enforces enterprise-grade security and compliance logging.

## Rationale
This architecture uses read-replicas and WAL-based CDC to protect write performance and achieve sub-800ms search requirements. All components, backups, and logs remain strictly within the `eu-central-1` region to satisfy EU data residency mandates.

Cache / Session Store.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries within the EU. The architecture utilizes an in-memory cache and session store to achieve sub-millisecond latency and meet high-performance search requirements.

## Key Elements
*   **Cache / Session Store Container:** Managed AWS ElastiCache for Redis 7.x Cluster Mode in `eu-central-1`.
*   **Session Store Component:** Manages active user authentication tokens and TTL-expiring keys.
*   **Hot Data Cache Component:** Caches frequent catalogue queries using a `volatile-lru` eviction policy.
*   **Distributed Lock Component:** Coordinates concurrency for circulation checkouts.
*   **API Gateway & Core Services Container:** External callers interacting with the cache container.

## Relationships
*   **API Gateway -> Session Store Component:** Validates active user sessions using RESP3 over TLS 1.3 with IAM authentication.
*   **Core Services Container -> Hot Data Cache Component:** Queries and invalidates cached catalogue data using RESP3 over TLS 1.3.
*   **Core Services Container -> Distributed Lock Component:** Acquires and releases concurrency locks using RESP3 over TLS 1.3.

## Technology Stack
*   **AWS ElastiCache for Redis 7.x (Cluster Mode):** Selected for in-memory data structures, native multi-AZ replication, and EU-Central-1 data residency.
*   **RESP3 over TLS 1.3:** Enforces secure encryption in transit for all container interactions.
*   **Redis ACLs & IAM Database Authentication:** Secures service-level access boundaries.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures sub-millisecond session validation and hot data caching to satisfy the 99th-percentile search response time under 800 ms. Strict adherence to AWS EU-Central-1 deployment and TLS 1.3 guarantees compliance with EU-only data residency constraints.

File Storage Container.analysis:
## Overview
[Component C4 architecture for the File Storage Container within the Library Management System, designed to securely manage digital asset cataloging while strictly enforcing EU data residency.]

## Key Elements
- File Controller / API Router (Spring WebFlux / Java)
- Presigned URL Generator
- Virus & Malware Scanner Service (ClamAV via FastAPI / Python)
- Storage Abstraction Manager (AWS SDK for Java)
- Audit Logging & Access Policy Enforcer (AWS IAM / CloudTrail)
- AWS S3 EU-Central (EU-Central-1 Region)

## Relationships
- Integration Service -> File Controller [HTTPS/REST]: Uploads/downloads digital assets and requests secure tokens
- File Controller -> Audit Logging & Access Policy Enforcer [In-Memory Java Call]: Validates IAM permissions and EU residency
- File Controller -> Presigned URL Generator [In-Memory]: Issues time-limited S3 upload/download tokens
- Presigned URL Generator -> AWS S3 EU-Central [HTTPS/SigV4]: Direct client data transfer
- File Controller -> Virus & Malware Scanner [Internal gRPC]: Triggers asynchronous security scan
- Virus & Malware Scanner -> Storage Abstraction Manager [Internal gRPC]: Signals clean scan status for quarantine-to-production promotion
- Storage Abstraction Manager -> AWS S3 EU-Central [HTTPS/SigV4]: Enforces AES-256 encryption-at-rest and bucket restrictions

## Technology Stack
- Spring WebFlux / Java: Non-blocking reactive streaming of metadata and API routing
- FastAPI / Python with ClamAV: Lightweight wrapper and daemon for secure virus/malware scanning
- AWS SDK for Java: Handles AWS S3 encryption-at-rest (AES-256) and IAM integration
- AWS S3 EU-Central-1: Ensures strict EU-only data residency and quarantine isolation

## Rationale
[This component architecture prevents network bottlenecks by offloading heavy binary transfers to direct S3 presigned URLs while ensuring robust security via ClamAV scanning and strict EU data residency enforcement.]
